assumptions_and_conditions: Numeric measurements have consistent units and coding. Mean and SD describe the observed sample; inference to a population needs an appropriate sampling design.
diagnostic_procedures: Check units, missingness, histogram or boxplot, and extreme observations. Compare mean with median and inspect whether observations represent the intended population.
if_violated: Outliers or skew can pull the mean and inflate SD; selection bias makes population generalizations misleading. Report robust summaries or stratified estimates if appropriate.
diagnostic_caveats: There is no normality requirement merely to report a mean or SD; an inference about a population requires additional design assumptions.

assumptions_and_conditions: Measurements are meaningfully ordered. Quantile calculation, missing-data handling, and the target population are specified.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect frequency distributions, missing values, ties, and extreme or censored values. Check that the sample and any survey weights match the target population.
if_violated: Unrepresentative sampling biases population quantiles; high concentrations of ties or censoring limit interpretability of interpolated quartiles.
diagnostic_caveats: Median and IQR describe a sample without requiring normality; they are not confidence intervals or causal estimates.

assumptions_and_conditions: Categories are defined consistently, mutually interpretable, and linked to a clear denominator; observations or survey weights must reflect the intended population.
diagnostic_procedures: Tabulate each category including missing and unknown responses. Audit denominators, coding, duplicate records, weights, and cells with few observations.
if_violated: Misclassification and inconsistent denominators distort percentages; selection bias prevents valid population prevalence claims.
diagnostic_caveats: A percentage alone does not establish precision. Use design-appropriate intervals and account for clustered or weighted samples if making inferences.

assumptions_and_conditions: Paired continuous measurements are meaningful; Pearson correlation measures linear association. Conventional small-sample significance tests usually assume independent pairs and bivariate normality.
diagnostic_procedures: Plot x against y, inspect curvature and influential points, and examine residual patterns if fitting a line. Assess independence by the study design and inspect distributional shape for small-sample inference.
if_violated: A few extremes or a curved association can distort the coefficient; dependence and distributional misspecification can invalidate standard p-values or intervals.
diagnostic_caveats: Correlation is not causation. For inference, bivariate normality can sometimes be relaxed with adequate samples or suitable resampling.

assumptions_and_conditions: Observations are paired and independent across sampling units for standard inference. Rank ordering is meaningful; a monotone trend is needed for a strong single-number summary.
diagnostic_procedures: Draw a scatterplot with ranks or smoothing, assess monotonicity, ties and influential clusters, and check whether repeated measurements were treated as independent.
if_violated: Nonmonotonic associations may give a near-zero Spearman coefficient despite a substantial relationship; many ties affect precision and test approximations.
diagnostic_caveats: Spearman correlation does not assume normal data or require a monotonic relation to be calculated; monotonicity matters to interpretation.

assumptions_and_conditions: Two groups contain independent sampling units; the response is continuous. Standard pooled t inference assumes similar within-group variances and approximately normal sampling errors.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect group-specific boxplots and Q-Q plots; calculate group SDs, inspect outliers, and assess independence from design. Variance tests can supplement but not replace visual review.
if_violated: Unequal variances, especially with unequal sample sizes, distort pooled t error rates; extreme skew or outliers can impair small-sample inference.
diagnostic_caveats: Normality concerns the within-group errors, not the pooled outcome distribution. Welch t-test avoids equal-variance assumptions.

assumptions_and_conditions: Groups contain independent sampling units; outcome is continuous. Welch inference allows unequal group variances but remains sensitive to severe skew and outliers in small samples.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect each group with boxplots and Q-Q plots, consider sample sizes and influential values, and check independence by study design.
if_violated: Severe skew, extreme observations, or dependence can undermine the reference t approximation and misleadingly narrow intervals.
diagnostic_caveats: Welch does not require equal group variances. Larger samples improve robustness but do not correct selection bias or dependence.

assumptions_and_conditions: Each participant contributes a valid matched pair; differences between pairs are independent. Approximate normality is needed for classical small-sample t inference on pair differences.
diagnostic_procedures: Compute within-pair differences, plot their histogram and Q-Q plot, inspect extreme differences, and verify pair identifiers.
if_violated: Incorrect pairing or dependent pairs invalidates uncertainty estimates; skewed differences and outliers can distort small-sample tests.
diagnostic_caveats: It is the distribution of paired differences, not each raw measurement, that is relevant to the normality check.

assumptions_and_conditions: Two independent groups, with an ordinal or continuous response and interpretable rankings. A location/median interpretation requires comparable distribution shapes.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect group ECDFs, boxplots and density shapes; check ties and independence. Compare spreads and skew before describing a median difference.
if_violated: Dependence invalidates the rank test. Differing shape or scale means a significant rank test need not imply different medians.
diagnostic_caveats: Mann-Whitney tests distributional ordering, not automatically equality of medians; use a location interpretation only under suitable conditions.

assumptions_and_conditions: Valid matched pairs with independent differences across participants. For the usual symmetric location-shift interpretation, the paired-difference distribution is approximately symmetric.
diagnostic_procedures: Plot paired differences with histogram and boxplot; inspect zero differences, ties, and symmetry around the center; verify pair matching.
if_violated: Asymmetric differences undermine a simple median-shift interpretation; incorrect pairing or interdependent pairs invalidates standard inference.
diagnostic_caveats: The Wilcoxon signed-rank test is not the same as a sign test, and does not require normal paired differences.

assumptions_and_conditions: Independent observations across groups with continuous outcome; roughly normal within-group errors and similar group variances for classical F inference.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect residuals versus fits and Q-Q plots, group SDs and outliers; assess unequal cell sizes and independence of sampling units.
if_violated: Heterogeneous variances combined with unequal sizes can distort F tests; strong departures and influential points affect results.
diagnostic_caveats: Normality concerns residuals rather than all pooled data. Welch ANOVA may suit markedly unequal variances.

assumptions_and_conditions: Two categorical factors define valid cells with independent observations, continuous outcome, reasonable cell sizes, and adequate residual model fit; classical tests assume roughly equal residual variances.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect design-cell counts, factor combinations, interaction plots, residual-versus-fit and Q-Q plots, and cell-specific spreads.
if_violated: Empty or sparse cells can make effects nonestimable; severe variance inequality or dependent observations can invalidate conventional F tests.
diagnostic_caveats: Interactions should be examined before interpreting marginal main effects. Factor coding and unbalanced designs affect interpretation.

assumptions_and_conditions: Repeated outcomes are linked by participant identifiers and independent across participants. Classical repeated-measures ANOVA assumes appropriate within-person covariance; sphericity matters with at least three within-subject levels.
diagnostic_procedures: Check visit counts and missingness, residual Q-Q plots, subject trajectories, and Mauchly or epsilon estimates for sphericity when within-subject factor has more than two levels.
if_violated: Unmodeled missing visits or within-person covariance can distort standard errors and F tests. Sphericity violations require suitable corrections or other models.
diagnostic_caveats: With exactly two repeated levels, sphericity is automatic. Mauchly test does not establish all assumptions.

assumptions_and_conditions: Participants are independent between groups but repeatedly measured within participant. Continuous outcome, meaningful group-by-time structure, suitable residual model and within-person covariance are required.
diagnostic_procedures: Verify participant IDs, group allocation, missing visits, subject trajectories and residual Q-Q plots; assess group-specific residual spreads. Check sphericity/epsilon only for at least three within-person levels.
if_violated: Ignoring unequal residual spread, correlated measures or informative missingness can misstate the group-by-time effect. Sphericity violations affect uncorrected repeated-measures F tests.
diagnostic_caveats: With two timepoints, sphericity is automatic. A significant interaction is not by itself proof of causality without an appropriate study design.

assumptions_and_conditions: Continuous outcome; correctly coded groups and covariates; approximately linear covariate-outcome relation, independent errors and, for conventional ANCOVA, comparable covariate slopes between groups.
diagnostic_procedures: Plot outcome against covariate by group, fit or inspect group-by-covariate interaction, residual Q-Q and residual-versus-fit plots, and examine baseline covariate overlap.
if_violated: Nonlinear associations or unequal slopes make an adjusted common group contrast misleading; poor overlap makes extrapolation unstable.
diagnostic_caveats: For randomized trials, choose adjustment covariates prospectively. Adjusting for post-treatment variables can bias causal comparisons.

assumptions_and_conditions: Independent groups and outcome values with meaningful ordering. Comparing group medians specifically requires similarly shaped distributions.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect ECDFs, boxplots, ties, group sizes and rank distributions; establish independent group assignment from design.
if_violated: Dependent observations invalidate ordinary p-values; different distribution shapes weaken interpretations as a median-only effect.
diagnostic_caveats: Kruskal-Wallis detects differences in rank distributions, not exclusively medians. Significant omnibus results do not identify which groups differ.

assumptions_and_conditions: Measurements form valid matched blocks or repeated units, with consistent condition ordering and valid within-block comparisons.
diagnostic_procedures: Check that each block has required observations or documented handling of missingness; inspect per-block ranks, ties, and condition order.
if_violated: Incomplete blocks may be dropped or require a different procedure; broken block matching or dependence across blocks invalidates standard inference.
diagnostic_caveats: Friedman is an omnibus rank test and does not identify which pairs of conditions differ without follow-up comparisons.

assumptions_and_conditions: Categories and counts are correctly defined, units are independent, and expected frequencies are sufficient for the selected chi-square approximation.
diagnostic_procedures: Build a contingency table with expected counts, inspect structural zeros, sparse cells, duplicates, and whether observations appear in multiple cells.
if_violated: Small expected counts impair asymptotic p-value accuracy; correlated observations produce incorrect uncertainty estimates.
diagnostic_caveats: No universal single expected-count threshold applies to every table. Exact or simulation-based procedures may be preferable for sparse data.

assumptions_and_conditions: Cross-tabulated counts come from independent observational units and a sampling scheme compatible with the exact conditional test.
diagnostic_procedures: Verify independent units, table orientation and fixed-margin assumptions, inspect zero cells and data collection design.
if_violated: Nonindependent observations or selection mechanisms can invalidate the inferential interpretation despite the exact p-value calculation.
diagnostic_caveats: Fisher exact test does not require large expected counts; exactness refers to its stated sampling model, not absence of bias.

assumptions_and_conditions: Predictor and mean outcome have a suitably linear relation; errors have appropriate dependence structure and variance; standard t and F inference uses an adequate error distribution.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect scatterplot, residual-versus-fit plot, Q-Q plot, residual spread and leverage/Cook distance; evaluate independence from time or cluster design.
if_violated: Curvature biases slope summaries, heteroskedasticity harms conventional standard errors, and influential observations may drive results.
diagnostic_caveats: Residual normality matters most for small-sample classical inference, not for defining the OLS estimates. Association is not causation.

assumptions_and_conditions: Correct functional form for each predictor; independent or appropriately modeled errors; full-rank design matrix without extreme collinearity.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect residual plots, partial residual plots, VIF or condition indices, leverage/Cook distance, and dependence or heteroskedasticity.
if_violated: Omitted nonlinear effects bias interpretation, collinearity destabilizes coefficients, and nonindependent errors invalidate ordinary standard errors.
diagnostic_caveats: No single VIF cut-off proves a model invalid. Adjusted associations need not be causal.

assumptions_and_conditions: Binary outcome with valid event coding; specified predictors and approximately linear relationships on logit scale for continuous terms; no complete separation.
diagnostic_procedures: Check outcome counts and events per modeled parameter, cross-tabs for separation, logit-linearity plots or spline checks, deviance residuals and calibration.
if_violated: Separation causes infinite or unstable coefficients; sparse events and logit misspecification distort intervals and predicted probabilities.
diagnostic_caveats: Normality of the binary outcome is not required. Adequate events per parameter depend on data, complexity and estimation strategy.

assumptions_and_conditions: Nonnegative integer event counts with correctly defined exposure times or offsets; Poisson mean-variance relation conditional on predictors and suitable dependence structure.
diagnostic_procedures: Check count frequencies, zero counts, deviance and Pearson dispersion, residuals versus fitted values, offsets, and within-unit clustering.
if_violated: Overdispersion gives overly narrow standard errors and false positives; excess zeros, unmodeled dependence, or omitted exposure offsets distort estimates.
diagnostic_caveats: Excess zeros alone do not prove a zero-inflated data-generating process; assess alternative count models and data collection.

assumptions_and_conditions: Observations have valid subject or cluster identifiers. Random-effects/correlation structure and conditional mean model are appropriate; Gaussian LMM inference typically assumes suitable conditional residual behavior.
diagnostic_procedures: Review repeated-measure structure and cluster counts, random-effect variance or singular-fit warnings, conditional residual versus fitted and Q-Q plots, and missingness patterns.
if_violated: Wrong grouping or covariance structure biases standard errors; few clusters weaken uncertainty estimates; informative missingness may bias longitudinal comparisons.
diagnostic_caveats: Normality of raw outcomes is not the requirement; examine conditional residuals. Missing-at-random assumptions cannot be demonstrated from observed data alone.

assumptions_and_conditions: Outcome family and link match the data; observations are correctly clustered with identifiable random effects and a plausible conditional mean/correlation structure.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect dispersion and zero patterns for count families, calibrated probabilities for binary families, simulation-based residuals, convergence and singularity flags, and cluster counts.
if_violated: Wrong family or link, sparse clusters or poorly identified random effects can bias coefficients or misstate uncertainty.
diagnostic_caveats: A converged fit does not guarantee valid model specification. Diagnostic expectations vary substantially across GLMM families.

assumptions_and_conditions: Multiple numerical variables contain meaningful shared variation; variable scaling is consistent with the analytic goal. Principal components are descriptive directions of variance.
diagnostic_procedures: Examine variable correlations, SDs and units, missingness, outliers, scree plot, explained variance, and loading stability under resampling.
if_violated: Poor scaling or a few extremes can dominate components; unstable loadings and weak shared structure undermine interpretation.
diagnostic_caveats: PCA does not assume a latent-variable measurement model, and high explained variance does not prove construct validity.

assumptions_and_conditions: Indicators share enough common covariance for a defensible factor model; factor count and rotation are justified and the model is identifiable.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect correlation or polychoric matrix as appropriate, KMO, Bartlett test as context, eigenvalues and parallel analysis, communalities, loadings and residual correlations.
if_violated: Weak factorability, too many factors or inadequate sample information produce unstable, poorly interpretable loadings.
diagnostic_caveats: Bartlett significance alone does not establish factorability; EFA explores structure and is not confirmatory evidence by itself.

assumptions_and_conditions: Train and evaluation records reflect deployment conditions; predictors exclude information unavailable at prediction time; tree complexity is tuned without test-set leakage.
diagnostic_procedures: Check data leakage and duplicates, use held-out or cross-validated error, compare training versus validation performance, inspect class-specific metrics and subgroup performance.
if_violated: Leakage or untuned deep trees yields exaggerated accuracy and poor generalization; imbalance can make accuracy misleading.
diagnostic_caveats: Decision trees make few distributional assumptions, but predictive validity still depends on sampling and validation design.

assumptions_and_conditions: Features and labels are valid; training/testing split protects against leakage and correlated record duplication; predictive context is sufficiently similar to deployment.
diagnostic_procedures: Use out-of-bag and independent test results appropriately, compare training and validation metrics, check imbalance, leakage, calibration and subgroup performance.
if_violated: Correlated data across splits or leakage exaggerates performance; class imbalance can conceal poor sensitivity.
diagnostic_caveats: Out-of-bag error is not a substitute for external validation when groups or time periods differ.

assumptions_and_conditions: Treated and comparison units have meaningfully comparable untreated outcome trends (parallel trends), no anticipation, and no unaccounted time-varying cointerventions that differentially affect groups.
diagnostic_procedures: Graph pre-intervention trends across multiple periods when available, examine pre-trend placebo or event-study estimates, composition changes, concurrent policies and potential spillovers.
if_violated: Differential preexisting trends, changing group composition or simultaneous interventions can make the DiD contrast noncausal.
diagnostic_caveats: With only one pre-intervention period, parallel trends cannot be empirically checked. Nonsignificant pretrend tests never prove the assumption.

assumptions_and_conditions: Variables have coherent categories and mutually interpretable row/column denominators; records are accurate and appropriately weighted when relevant.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect contingency-table totals, zeros, duplicate records, category definitions, missingness and row/column/overall percentages.
if_violated: Miscoding and inconsistent denominators lead to misleading summaries, especially where sample sizes differ across groups.
diagnostic_caveats: Cross-tabulation is descriptive; significance or causal interpretation requires a separate inferential analysis and design.

assumptions_and_conditions: The population quantity (estimand), estimator and interval procedure are specified. Sampling, dependence and distributional conditions must support the claimed coverage.
diagnostic_procedures: Verify standard error calculation or bootstrap design, inspect sampling weights, clusters, small-cell counts, skew and boundary estimates; simulate coverage when feasible.
if_violated: Ignoring dependence, selective sampling or skew can produce intervals that undercover the target quantity.
diagnostic_caveats: A 95% frequentist confidence interval is a procedure with nominal long-run coverage, not a 95% probability the fixed parameter lies in this observed interval.

assumptions_and_conditions: Paired variables have a meaningful order; units are independent for classical inference. Ties and concordance definition should match the tau variant.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect scatterplot and ranking ties; confirm whether tau-b or another variant is used, and whether repeated subjects require clustered inference.
if_violated: Ignoring ties changes magnitude and variance; dependence leads to incorrect p-values.
diagnostic_caveats: Kendall tau summarizes ordinal concordance, not linear slope or causation.

assumptions_and_conditions: One variable is genuinely binary and the other continuous; independent sampling units and consistent binary coding.
diagnostic_procedures: Check group coding and sizes, within-group distributions, outliers and independence; compare with the equivalent two-group mean comparison.
if_violated: Severe outliers or coding errors distort correlation; dependent measures invalidate standard inference.
diagnostic_caveats: Point-biserial correlation measures association with a binary indicator, not a causal treatment effect by itself.

assumptions_and_conditions: Two target variables and relevant adjustment covariates are correctly specified. Standard partial correlation assumes an appropriate residual association model and independent units.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect pairwise and residual scatterplots, nonlinear patterns, collinearity, influence points and rationale for covariate selection.
if_violated: Missed nonlinear effects or inappropriate covariate control produce misleading partial associations, potentially opening collider bias.
diagnostic_caveats: Covariate choice is a causal-design judgment and cannot be validated by goodness-of-fit tests alone.

assumptions_and_conditions: Independent observations with a continuous outcome and a prespecified reference mean; small-sample classical t inference assumes roughly normal population errors.
diagnostic_procedures: Review histogram/Q-Q plot, outliers, sampling independence, sample size and the origin of the reference value.
if_violated: Outliers or strong skew can distort small-sample inference; dependence invalidates the usual standard error.
diagnostic_caveats: The reference mean should not be chosen after seeing the data without accounting for selection.

assumptions_and_conditions: Independent groups with a continuous outcome. Welch ANOVA allows heterogeneous group variances but still needs suitable within-group sampling behavior.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect group boxplots and Q-Q plots, group sizes, outliers and independence; compare within-group spreads.
if_violated: Strong outliers, severe small-group skew or dependence can distort Welch F inference.
diagnostic_caveats: Welch ANOVA does not require equal variances; omnibus significance does not identify which groups differ.

assumptions_and_conditions: Two or more continuous outcomes, independent sampling units, reasonably well-specified multivariate error structure, and group covariance behavior compatible with the chosen test.
diagnostic_procedures: Check multivariate outliers, residual correlation and Q-Q diagnostics, cell counts, covariance matrices (Box M cautiously), and singularity among outcomes.
if_violated: Sparse cells, nonnormal multivariate residuals or strongly differing covariance matrices can distort classical multivariate F approximations.
diagnostic_caveats: Pillai trace is often more robust than some alternatives but does not remove all design or covariance problems.

assumptions_and_conditions: Binary responses occur in correctly matched pairs and sampling pairs are independent. Discordant pairs provide the information for McNemar inference.
diagnostic_procedures: Construct a paired 2x2 table, verify subject matching, count discordant pairs and choose exact or asymptotic method accordingly.
if_violated: Very few discordant pairs make large-sample chi-square approximations inaccurate; mispaired responses make inference invalid.
diagnostic_caveats: McNemar targets marginal discordance rather than an ordinary two-independent-samples association.

assumptions_and_conditions: Continuous predictor and outcome support an adequately specified polynomial mean relation; errors and sampling structure support the chosen regression inference.
diagnostic_procedures: Plot outcome against predictor, residual patterns, leverage at range extremes, compare degrees using validation or nested tests, and inspect overfitting.
if_violated: High-degree fits can oscillate and extrapolate wildly; misspecified curvature and outliers bias interpretation.
diagnostic_caveats: Polynomial coefficients depend on scaling and centering; predictions beyond observed predictor range are especially fragile.

assumptions_and_conditions: Selected smooth terms represent plausible relationships; smoothing parameters, error family/link and dependence structure suit the data.
diagnostic_procedures: Review estimated smooths with confidence bands, basis-dimension diagnostics, effective degrees of freedom, residual plots and out-of-sample performance.
if_violated: Under-smoothing overfits; excessive smoothing hides nonlinear effects; wrong family or residual dependence affects inference.
diagnostic_caveats: A flexible smooth does not remove confounding. Basis checks and smoothness selection are separate issues.

assumptions_and_conditions: Outcome has at least three nominal categories with correctly defined reference class; class frequencies and predictors support identifiable coefficients.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect category frequencies, separation and sparse predictor-category cells, convergence, calibration, and multinomial residual or predictive checks.
if_violated: Sparse classes or separation make estimates unstable; class misclassification and omitted structure impair fit.
diagnostic_caveats: Independence-of-irrelevant-alternatives assumptions arise in certain multinomial choice applications; suitability depends on the interpretation and data structure.

assumptions_and_conditions: Outcome categories have meaningful order; standard cumulative-logit model assumes proportional odds (common covariate effect across cutpoints), with adequate observations per level.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect category frequencies, proportional-odds diagnostics and threshold-specific effects; check sparse cells, convergence and predicted-category calibration.
if_violated: A strong proportional-odds violation makes one common odds ratio misleading; empty categories produce unstable estimates.
diagnostic_caveats: The proportional-odds assumption pertains to the standard cumulative-logit form; other ordinal link models impose different assumptions.

assumptions_and_conditions: Nonnegative counts and appropriate exposure offsets; conditional count variance can exceed its mean and dependence is appropriately handled.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect mean-variance relation, Pearson residual dispersion, zero frequency, fitted versus observed count distributions and offset correctness.
if_violated: Incorrect dispersion or unmodeled structural zeros can bias fit and uncertainty; forgetting exposure time invalidates rates.
diagnostic_caveats: Negative binomial handles a particular form of overdispersion; it is not automatically preferred for all zero-heavy datasets.

assumptions_and_conditions: Counts include a defensible separate structural-zero mechanism and a sampling count process; both model components are identifiable from the study design and covariates.
diagnostic_procedures: Compare observed and fitted zero counts, inspect simulation-based residuals and convergence, consider hurdle or ordinary count alternatives, and assess component interpretability.
if_violated: Without an identifiable extra-zero process, zero-inflated parameters are unstable or misleading; misspecification distorts counts and predicted zeros.
diagnostic_caveats: Many observed zeros alone do not establish structural zero inflation. Non-nested comparisons require care.

assumptions_and_conditions: Outcome is a continuous proportion strictly between zero and one for ordinary beta regression; mean-link and precision/dispersion model suit the data.
diagnostic_procedures: Check observed zero/one values, fitted mean-variance patterns, quantile or simulation-based residuals and dispersion changes.
if_violated: Boundary observations are outside the ordinary beta likelihood; wrong precision specification may distort uncertainty.
diagnostic_caveats: Do not silently replace exact 0 or 1 values with arbitrary nearby numbers; use a justified boundary-aware model or design.

assumptions_and_conditions: Quantile level is prespecified; conditional quantile function has an appropriate predictor form and inference reflects dependence/heteroskedasticity.
diagnostic_procedures: Plot fitted quantiles against data, compare slopes across quantiles, check sparse tails and influence, and use appropriate bootstrap/resampling units.
if_violated: Misspecified conditional quantile relations or naive standard errors can bias interpretation, especially in tails or clustered data.
diagnostic_caveats: Quantile regression does not require normally distributed errors, but its coefficient interpretation differs from mean regression.

assumptions_and_conditions: Clusters are independent across units, correlated outcomes within clusters are correctly assigned, and mean/link model is suitable; robust sandwich inference needs sufficient independent clusters.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect cluster size distribution, working correlation estimates, residuals and dispersion; check the number of independent clusters and sensitivity to correlation structure.
if_violated: Few clusters can make sandwich standard errors unreliable; wrong mean model biases marginal effects.
diagnostic_caveats: GEE estimates population-averaged associations; robust SE does not repair wrong mean models or confounding.

assumptions_and_conditions: Event times and censoring status are correctly recorded with valid time origin; standard Cox model assumes proportional hazards and conditionally noninformative censoring.
diagnostic_procedures: Plot Schoenfeld residuals against time, inspect log-minus-log curves when helpful, assess functional form via residuals, and review censoring patterns and time origin.
if_violated: Nonproportional hazards makes a single hazard ratio time dependent; informative censoring and incorrect time origin bias hazard estimates.
diagnostic_caveats: A nonsignificant proportional-hazards test does not prove proportionality; censoring ignorability is not testable from observed outcomes alone.

assumptions_and_conditions: Event times, origin and status are correct; censoring is independent of the event process conditional on design, and subjects are appropriately sampled.
diagnostic_procedures: Audit event/censor coding and time origin; plot numbers at risk and censoring, check staggered entry and competing events.
if_violated: Informative censoring biases survival probabilities; competing risks make 1 minus Kaplan-Meier survival unsuitable as a cause-specific cumulative incidence estimate.
diagnostic_caveats: Kaplan-Meier does not require proportional hazards. Independent censoring is a substantive assumption, not proven by a plotted curve.

assumptions_and_conditions: Independent groups have comparable event and censoring definitions; censoring is conditionally noninformative. Ordinary log-rank is most powerful under approximately proportional hazards.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect Kaplan-Meier curves, numbers at risk, censoring by group and potential crossing curves; check ties and event counts.
if_violated: Informative censoring or incorrect grouping biases inference; crossing hazards can reduce power or obscure time-specific differences.
diagnostic_caveats: Noncrossing/proportional hazards is not required for the log-rank statistic to be computed; it affects the test power and summary interpretation.

assumptions_and_conditions: The factor structure is specified before model fitting; model is identifiable, measurement scales/estimators are appropriate, and sample information supports estimation.
diagnostic_procedures: Check identification and convergence, standardized loadings, residual covariance, fit indices (CFI, TLI, RMSEA, SRMR) and distribution-sensitive estimation.
if_violated: Misidentification or incompatible estimators prevent meaningful interpretation; poor fit or weak loadings undermine the proposed measurement model.
diagnostic_caveats: Good global fit alone does not prove construct validity or measurement invariance across groups.

assumptions_and_conditions: A path diagram and direction of associations are theoretically justified and identifiable; exogenous confounding is addressed when paths are interpreted causally.
diagnostic_procedures: Review identification, convergence, residual covariances, model fit, path stability, and sensitivity to plausible omitted confounders.
if_violated: Omitted causes or incorrect directionality can yield biased causal paths even if global fit looks acceptable.
diagnostic_caveats: Statistical fit cannot establish causal direction; cross-sectional path models are especially vulnerable to equivalent alternative models.

assumptions_and_conditions: Measurement and structural relations are specified, identified and estimable with a suitable estimator and adequate sample information.
diagnostic_procedures: Check convergence, parameter identification, factor loadings, residuals, CFI/TLI, RMSEA and SRMR, plus sensitivity to alternative structures.
if_violated: Weak identification or misspecification can lead to unstable parameters and invalid substantive interpretations.
diagnostic_caveats: Fit cutoffs are context dependent and should not be treated as universal proof of validity or causal identification.

assumptions_and_conditions: Exposure precedes mediator, which precedes outcome. Causal mediation requires no unmeasured exposure-outcome, mediator-outcome or exposure-mediator confounding under the chosen estimand; no relevant post-exposure mediator-outcome confounder under conventional identification.
diagnostic_procedures: Audit variable timing and causal diagram, pre-exposure covariates, mediator-outcome confounding candidates, positivity, and run sensitivity analyses for unmeasured confounding.
if_violated: Violations of sequential exchangeability can make indirect-effect estimates biased or uninterpretable as causal mediation.
diagnostic_caveats: No diagnostic test proves mediator-outcome exchangeability; an observed association through a mediator is not automatically a causal indirect effect.

assumptions_and_conditions: Repeated measures align to a meaningful time scale; trajectory functional form and growth-factor structure are identifiable with suitable missing-data assumptions.
diagnostic_procedures: Plot subject trajectories, inspect time coding and loading constraints, test alternative growth forms, review model fit, and examine attrition patterns.
if_violated: Wrong trajectory shape or selective dropout can misstate average growth and between-person variability.
diagnostic_caveats: Growth curves do not by themselves establish causal effects. Measurement invariance may matter for latent constructs measured over time.

assumptions_and_conditions: Time observations are ordered at a stable frequency; differenced model is approximately stationary as required and residual innovations are adequately uncorrelated for the fitted ARIMA.
diagnostic_procedures: Plot series and ACF/PACF, review differencing and seasonality, inspect residual ACF and Ljung-Box statistics, and use rolling-origin forecast tests.
if_violated: Unremoved trend/seasonality or residual autocorrelation signals misspecification and unreliable intervals/forecasts.
diagnostic_caveats: Stationarity applies to the modeled transformed or differenced process, not necessarily the original observed series.

assumptions_and_conditions: Time series has a form of level, trend or seasonality supported by chosen ETS components and a suitable error specification.
diagnostic_procedures: Review decomposition/seasonal plots, residual ACF, forecast errors, component plausibility and rolling-origin validation.
if_violated: Wrong seasonal/trend components or autocorrelated residuals degrade forecast accuracy and interval calibration.
diagnostic_caveats: Multiplicative ETS specifications usually require positive values; an apparent trend is not guaranteed to persist in forecasting.

assumptions_and_conditions: Intervention time is defensible with enough pre/post observations; counterfactual trend/seasonality and autocorrelation are modeled and major simultaneous changes considered.
diagnostic_procedures: Graph long pre/post series, check intervention-date sensitivity, residual ACF, secular trend, seasonal structure and cointerventions or measurement changes.
if_violated: Misspecified baseline trends, serial correlation or concurrent policies can create spurious interruption effects.
diagnostic_caveats: Interrupted time series provides stronger quasi-experimental evidence with multiple observations, but cannot fully rule out concurrent causes.

assumptions_and_conditions: Treatment assignment is conditionally exchangeable given measured pre-treatment covariates, with positivity/overlap and a defensible treatment model.
diagnostic_procedures: Plot propensity score overlap, inspect standardized mean differences after weighting/matching, extreme weights, effective sample size, and covariate missingness.
if_violated: Poor overlap and unstable weights inflate variance or change the estimand; unmeasured confounding biases estimated treatment effects.
diagnostic_caveats: Balance diagnostics cannot establish absence of unmeasured confounding. Removing nonoverlap may change the target population.

assumptions_and_conditions: Predictor information is available at prediction time; all tuning is isolated from final evaluation, and training/test distributions approximate intended use.
diagnostic_procedures: Check leakage, time/participant split boundaries, training versus validation errors, tuning stability, calibration and subgroup metrics.
if_violated: Leakage and excessive hyperparameter searching inflate accuracy; drift or imbalance harms deployment performance.
diagnostic_caveats: Strong in-sample fit is not evidence of predictive validity; use honest external or out-of-sample validation.

assumptions_and_conditions: The chosen regression family/link is appropriate; predictors and penalty are scaled consistently, and regularization strength is selected without test-set leakage.
diagnostic_procedures: Check standardization, cross-validated lambda, holdout error, residual diagnostics for model family and coefficient stability.
if_violated: Poor scaling gives unequal penalties; wrong family or tuning leakage reduces predictive validity.
diagnostic_caveats: Ridge shrinks coefficients but generally does not select them to exact zero. Penalties change traditional coefficient inference.

assumptions_and_conditions: Response family/link is suitable; predictors have consistent scaling, and lambda selection respects validation and dependence structure.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect standardized predictors, cross-validation folds, model stability across folds, validation error and correlated features.
if_violated: Improper scaling or unstable tuning produces fragile variable selection and unreliable prediction.
diagnostic_caveats: LASSO variable selection is unstable among correlated predictors; naive post-selection p-values are generally invalid.

assumptions_and_conditions: Model family/link is appropriate; predictor scaling and elastic-net mixing/penalty parameters are selected through leak-free validation.
diagnostic_procedures: Check cross-validation for alpha and lambda, standardized predictors, coefficient stability and out-of-sample errors.
if_violated: Poor tuning or inconsistent scaling compromises prediction; unmodeled dependence invalidates ordinary random folds.
diagnostic_caveats: Coefficient selection does not independently establish causality or conventional confidence intervals.

assumptions_and_conditions: Predictor scaling, kernel and penalty settings are chosen appropriately for the objective; evaluation is separated from tuning.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect scaled feature ranges, kernel/regularization grid, training versus validation performance, class imbalance, calibration and leakage.
if_violated: Poor scaling or kernel tuning makes boundaries unstable and out-of-sample accuracy optimistic.
diagnostic_caveats: SVM does not generally provide calibrated probabilities without an additional calibration step.

assumptions_and_conditions: Chosen distance metric reflects meaningful similarity; features are scaled compatibly and neighborhood size k is tuned without leakage.
diagnostic_procedures: Check standardized feature ranges, sparse/high-dimensional effects, sensitivity across k, class balance, and held-out predictive performance.
if_violated: Dominant units, wrong distance or small k amplify noise; very large k oversmooths local structure.
diagnostic_caveats: Curse-of-dimensionality can weaken neighbor interpretation even when code runs successfully.

assumptions_and_conditions: Class priors and feature likelihood models are plausible; naive Bayes approximates conditional independence of features within each class.
diagnostic_procedures: Review feature dependence within classes, predicted versus observed probabilities, prior prevalence and held-out class-wise performance.
if_violated: Strong within-class dependence or misspecified likelihoods may yield poorly calibrated probabilities.
diagnostic_caveats: Conditional independence is an approximation, not a guarantee; useful classification can occur despite violation.

assumptions_and_conditions: Network architecture and capacity are commensurate with data volume; preprocessing, tuning and final validation are separated to avoid leakage.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect training and validation loss curves, overfitting gaps, hyperparameter sensitivity, calibration, subgroup errors and performance on a true holdout.
if_violated: Excessive network capacity overfits and performs poorly on new samples; distribution drift undermines generalization.
diagnostic_caveats: Training convergence does not establish stable performance, interpretability or causal identification.

assumptions_and_conditions: Numeric features have meaningful distance and scaling; approximately compact cluster structure is suitable for Euclidean centroid partitions.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect feature scales/outliers, cluster sizes, inertia/elbow, silhouette, multiple random starts and stability under resampling.
if_violated: Poor scaling and outliers distort centroids; elongated or unequal-density clusters can be misrepresented.
diagnostic_caveats: Silhouette or elbow plots do not prove natural clusters exist. The chosen k is an analytic decision.

assumptions_and_conditions: Distance and linkage method reflect substantive similarity; preprocessing handles mixed scales, missingness and unusual observations appropriately.
diagnostic_procedures: Check distance scaling, dendrogram stability, linkage sensitivity, cophenetic correlation and resampling robustness.
if_violated: Unstable distances/linkages or outliers can induce arbitrary splits and misleading dendrogram structure.
diagnostic_caveats: A dendrogram always yields branches even if the population has no natural clusters.

assumptions_and_conditions: Distance metric and density parameters suit scaled features; clusters are expected to form locally dense regions separated by sparser regions.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect k-distance curve, sensitivity to epsilon/minPts and scaling, proportion labeled noise, and stability across parameter choices.
if_violated: Wrong radius or scaling merges distinct clusters or marks legitimate records as noise; variable-density populations can be poorly represented.
diagnostic_caveats: DBSCAN labels points as noise according to density choices, not because they are necessarily errors or anomalies.

assumptions_and_conditions: Anomalies are comparatively rare and distinguishable by isolation in the chosen feature space; reference training sample reflects intended baseline population.
diagnostic_procedures: Check feature quality, contamination assumptions, anomalous-score stability, validation against known cases if available, and subgroup false-positive rates.
if_violated: Nonrepresentative reference data or shifting populations cause high false alerts; correlated feature artifacts can dominate scores.
diagnostic_caveats: An anomaly score flags unusual records, not confirmed fraud, illness, or data error.

assumptions_and_conditions: Exposure precedes the modeled response lags; lag window, exposure-response basis, time trend and confounders are prespecified or justified; temporal dependence and outcome family are suitably modeled.
diagnostic_procedures: Inspect exposure and outcome time alignment, plausible lag ranges, seasonal/trend controls, basis dimensions, concurvity, residual ACF and sensitivity to lag/basis choices.
if_violated: Time misalignment, undercontrolled seasonality or poorly chosen lag bases produce spurious cumulative or delayed associations.
diagnostic_caveats: DLNM coefficients and cumulative effects are sensitive to basis specification; lagged association does not by itself identify causality.
